title: Household Cleaners Growth
prompt: Your client is a global consumer packaged goods company, Grime Co. It makes paper products such as paper towels, home cleaning products, and laundry care products. The Board has set an aggressive revenue target of $2B four years from now; current revenue is $1B. The CEO has asked you to evaluate the company's position and develop a strategy to deliver $2B in top-line results in four years.

clarifying_info.answer: Grime Co. has a strong stance in favor of sustainability.
Sales are divided evenly across paper products, home cleaning products, and laundry care products, about 33% each.
Net sales equal retail sales minus trade spend, which manufacturers pay distributors or retailers to incentivize sell-through.
Maintaining market share as the market grows will raise sales to $1.5B in four years; growth is similar across all three categories.

interviewer_notes: This Bain-style case requires market growth, organic growth through a new product, and inorganic growth through one acquisition. Strong candidates track the remaining revenue gap after every lever. Other organic options are unavailable, so steer to the toilet cleaner. Grime Co. can buy only one of Organoclean and Home Defense; the answer must combine projected sales with distribution and values synergies.

suggested_framework.summary: Book framework separates baseline market growth, organic initiatives, and inorganic growth.

children.label: Test sustainability, brand, and culture fit

stages.interviewer_asks: How would you structure Grime Co.'s options for reaching $2B in four years?
stages.expected_answer: Separate the $1B growth requirement into baseline market growth, organic growth, and inorganic growth. Track the gap after each lever. Organic options include pricing, marketing, distribution, and new products; acquisitions must be tested for financial contribution and strategic fit.
good_answer_signals: Uses market, organic, and inorganic buckets

stages.interviewer_asks: Market growth will bring Grime Co. to $1.5B. What does the planned toilet cleaner contribute, and what gap remains?
stages.info_to_release: The product launches in year three, sells for $5, incurs 20% trade spend, and is expected to sell 40M units per year.
stages.expected_answer: The target gap after market growth is $500M. Net price is $4 after trade spend, so 40M units add $160M of net sales and leave a $340M gap.
good_answer_signals: Uses net rather than retail sales
Recognizes that an inorganic lever is still required

stages.interviewer_asks: Based on Exhibit 1, what will each acquisition target's sales be in four years?
stages.release_when: After the candidate identifies acquisition as the remaining growth lever.
stages.info_to_release: Grime Co. can acquire only one target. Round four-year sales to the nearest $10M.
stages.expected_answer: Organoclean grows from $150M at 10% to $219.615M, rounded to $220M. Home Defense grows from $200M at 20% to $414.72M, rounded to $410M. Home Defense closes the headline gap, but synergies and product fit must be considered.
good_answer_signals: Does not automatically choose the larger target

stages.interviewer_asks: What other factors should Grime Co. consider when choosing between the acquisitions?
stages.info_to_release: Organoclean can gain $40M of European sales in year one, tripling to $120M in year four. Twenty-five percent of Home Defense sales are harmful bug killers that Grime Co. will not sell and that cannot be reformulated.
stages.expected_answer: Consider distribution, procurement, manufacturing, back-office, co-branding, and scale synergies against values clash, brand dilution, culture mismatch, and antitrust. Organoclean adds $220M plus $120M of European sales, exactly closing the $340M gap. Home Defense loses $102.5M of its $410M, leaving a $32.5M gap. Organoclean is the better fit.
good_answer_signals: Connects Organoclean to Grime Co.'s values

stages.interviewer_asks: What should Grime Co. do to reach its target?
stages.expected_answer: Use market growth to reach $1.5B, launch the toilet cleaner for $160M, and acquire Organoclean. Its $220M projected sales plus $120M European synergy closes the gap and fits Grime Co.'s sustainability stance. Verify assumptions, value and contact the target, plan diligence and integration, and execute the product launch. Risks include price, profitability, growth uncertainty, and rapid expansion.
good_answer_signals: Explains why fit beats Home Defense's headline size
Includes valuation and integration next steps

exhibits.title: Two acquisition targets
exhibits.description: Products, current sales, annual growth, and four-year compound sales for Organoclean and Home Defense Inc.
exhibits.key_insight: Home Defense is larger, but Organoclean's distribution synergy and sustainability fit make it the only target that reaches the goal without discarding products.

math.question: What does the new product contribute?
Which target closes the $340M gap after synergies?
math.answer: Organoclean closes the gap; Home Defense leaves $32.5M

synthesis: Grime Co. should combine market growth, the new toilet cleaner, and acquisition of Organoclean. Market growth reaches $1.5B and the product adds $160M, leaving $340M. Organoclean's $220M projected sales and $120M European synergy close the gap and fit Grime Co.'s values; Home Defense leaves $32.5M after removing bug killers. Verify assumptions, value and contact Organoclean, and plan diligence and integration.
what_great_looks_like: Tracks the revenue gap after each lever
Uses net sales after trade spend
Evaluates fit before choosing the larger target
common_pitfalls: Choosing Home Defense solely on size
Ignoring bug-killer losses and Organoclean synergies
